clue.text: Not against being involved with an opponent

indicators.note: involved here means tangled up, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone declines to oppose a rival they have become entangled with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being involved' turns the ten letters of NOT AGAINST into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is an adversary, the one who works against you.

explanation.surface: A fool finds himself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is old slang for a fool, and noodles are the strips of pasta floating in a bowl of broth.

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape or make, so the letters are refashioned into another word

explanation.surface: Someone teases the trendy lover of a pretty girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' reworks the letters of TEASE THE; it looks like an adjective describing the admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person devoted to art and loveliness.

parts.note: a matter settled is finished, over and done
a tax is a charge levied on people

explanation.surface: A war profiteer has paid off his tax bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To profiteer is to make excessive gains by asking too much money for goods.

explanation.surface: A batsman not dismissed, or a student confined to college.
explanation.walkthrough: At British schools and universities to be gated is to be confined to the premises as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not out of the house is inside it, and a student kept within the college walls stays inside too.

explanation.surface: A thief grabs something and is shot for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal is to make off with something; a film director gets a shot of a scene in one filmed attempt.

clue.text: Having cut down gradually, in time died an abstainer

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another, so the abstainer goes into the word for time

parts.note: a while is a period of time
TT, teetotal, describes someone abstaining from alcohol
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A man who cut back slowly on drink finally died teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Whittled means pared down bit by bit, like wood shaved with a knife.

clue.text: Sanctity of many a note written in sorrow

indicators.note: the letters are put down inside another word, as if inscribed within it

parts.note: sadness is sorrow
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Something holy is found in a sad note of a dirge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is the quality of being holy.

indicators.note: the yarns go around, enclosing the other word

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or yarns
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl surrounded by tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a female first name.

clue.text: Greedily takes the foam from the cask

parts.note: to hog something is to grab it all for yourself
the head on a beer is its froth

explanation.surface: A drinker greedily skims the froth off a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large barrel for wine or beer.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible version of these letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An olive tree and a rose that flowered late.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster is a shrub also called wild olive or Russian olive.

indicators.note: pronounced says that what is wanted sounds like the word spoken

parts.note: a peak is the top of a mountain

explanation.surface: A dog declared best in show.
explanation.definitionFit: A peke is a Pekingese, a small long-haired breed.

clue.text: Sober up, or I may be forced to give tips

indicators.note: the letters may be forced out of shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk is told to sober up or he will have to hand out gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be forced' rearranges SOBER UP OR I into the French word for tips.
explanation.definitionFit: Pourboire is French for a gratuity, literally money for a drink, used in English too.

parts.note: firm means hard
someone who boiled became furiously worked up

explanation.surface: A clever company got stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-boiled means tough and worldly-wise, not easily fooled.

clue.text: One way to ensure cleaner play

definitions.text: One way to ensure cleaner play

parts.words: One way to ensure cleaner play
parts.note: not a sporting fair-play rule: it means cutting rude passages out of a stage play, as Thomas Bowdler did with Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A method for making a game fairer.
explanation.definitionFit: To expurgate a text is to remove anything coarse, as Thomas Bowdler did in his Family Shakespeare.

parts.note: refers to the Ode on a Grecian Urn: melodies heard are sweet, but the silent ones are sweeter

explanation.surface: Describing the tunes the poet liked best.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet praised silent music never reaching the ear, the pipes on the urn playing to the spirit.

parts.note: old Dutch is cockney slang for a wife, from Dutch plate rhyming with mate; the clue asks what a German would call her

explanation.surface: Something ancient and Dutch found in southern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Dutch is cockney slang for a wife, as in 'my old Dutch'; Bavaria is a German region, so the German word for housewife is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Hausfrau is German for a housewife or wife.

clue.text: Wrap up baby son with shuffling gait

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
a waddle is a clumsy rocking walk

explanation.surface: A parent bundles up a little boy who walks unsteadily.
explanation.definitionFit: To swaddle an infant is to bind it tightly in cloth.

parts.note: dead means flat or lifeless, dull
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A headteacher who never does anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadness is lifelessness, a state with no movement or energy.

explanation.surface: A seafood dish that its admirers know well.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish is eaten as seafood, and its ribbed shell is fan-shaped, a pattern known as scalloping.

parts.note: blue means smutty or indecent
a pencil is something you write with

explanation.surface: Ban a writer of smut.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors marked cuts with a coloured crayon, so to cut or censor text came to be called this.

clue.text: Wiles that give rise to some heart-searching

indicators.note: some of the following letters are taken, a run lying within the word

explanation.surface: Tricks that lead to a good deal of soul-searching.
explanation.definitionFit: Arts in the sense of cunning devices or stratagems, as in feminine arts.

clue.text: Where, in a town, my dear love twice sat down

definitions.text: Where, in a town, my dear love twice sat down

parts.words: Where, in a town, my dear love twice sat down
parts.note: a romantic-sounding place where a sweetheart rested: in fact a public house where one sits down to drink

explanation.surface: Recalling the spot in town where a lover rested twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house, a place to sit and drink.

clue.text: After doing well, a student becomes irregular

parts.note: a player doing well is in form
L is a learner driver's plate, so a student

explanation.surface: A student who has done well starts behaving casually.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means not following official rules or formal regularity, unofficial.

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the word is turned around

parts.note: to deem is to judge or consider

explanation.surface: Payment for a judge is increased.
explanation.definitionFit: Meed is an archaic word for a reward or due payment.

clue.text: Hung around to see Italian communist about note

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
I is the abbreviation for Italian (and the international car code for Italy)
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: Someone loitered to meet an Italian Communist about a message.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly, standing about with no purpose.

clue.text: Pass drinks in surroundings of ease, say

indicators.note: the drinks are placed inside the other letters
the surroundings of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: laps means drinks, as a cat laps milk

explanation.surface: Pass round the drinks to put guests at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or slips by.

parts.note: to depress is to dishearten or discourage
the ant is a social insect, and a worker ant is one of its caste

explanation.surface: Persuading a social worker to stay off drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A depressant is a sedative drug that slows down the body's functions.
